title: "GDP_PPP"
author: "XuZhi Wang"
date: "2026-04-26"
output: pdf_document
---

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# STEP 1: Load PPP data from World Bank CSV file
ppp <- read.csv(
  "API_PA.NUS.PPP_DS2_en_csv_v2_1331.csv",
  skip = 4
)

# STEP 2: Convert PPP data from wide format to long format
ppp_long <- ppp %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("X"),
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "ppp_lcu_per_intd"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(sub("X", "", year))
  )

# STEP 3: Define selected countries
selected_countries <- c(
  # Main study countries
  "United Kingdom",
  "China",
  "South Africa",
  "United States",
  "India",
  "Mexico",
  "Korea, Rep.",
  
  # EU-27 countries
  "Austria",
  "Belgium",
  "Bulgaria",
  "Croatia",
  "Cyprus",
  "Czechia",
  "Denmark",
  "Estonia",
  "Finland",
  "France",
  "Germany",
  "Greece",
  "Hungary",
  "Ireland",
  "Italy",
  "Latvia",
  "Lithuania",
  "Luxembourg",
  "Malta",
  "Netherlands",
  "Poland",
  "Portugal",
  "Romania",
  "Slovak Republic",
  "Slovenia",
  "Spain",
  "Sweden"
)

# STEP 4: Extract selected countries for 2018 and 2017
ppp_selected <- ppp_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    year %in% c(2018, 2017),
    Country.Name %in% selected_countries
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    country_name = Country.Name,
    country_code = Country.Code,
    indicator_name = Indicator.Name,
    indicator_code = Indicator.Code,
    year,
    ppp_lcu_per_intd
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(country_name, year)

# STEP 5: Check results
ppp_selected

# Check number of countries by year
table(ppp_selected$year)

# STEP 6: Export selected PPP data
write.csv(
  ppp_selected,
  "diabetes_project_ppp_2017_2018_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
